title: Preparation for Calculus
intro: Algebra, graphs, functions and radians provide the language used throughout the course.
prerequisites: No calculus required. Review algebra and basic geometry as needed.

sectionTitles.P.2: Linear Models and Rates of Change

title: Limits and Their Properties
intro: Understand nearby behavior, one-sided limits, continuity and unbounded behavior before defining a derivative.
prerequisites: Preparation unit: function domains, algebra and trigonometry.

title: Differentiation
intro: Build derivatives from limits, then calculate rates using rules, implicit relations and time-dependent geometry.

sectionTitles.2.1: The Derivative and the Tangent Line Problem
sectionTitles.2.2: Basic Differentiation Rules and Rates of Change
sectionTitles.2.3: Product and Quotient Rules and Higher-Order Derivatives

title: Applications of Differentiation
intro: Use derivatives to justify graph shape, extrema, approximations and numerical root finding.
prerequisites: Unit 2: derivative rules and tangent lines.

sectionTitles.3.2: Rolle’s Theorem and the Mean Value Theorem
sectionTitles.3.3: Increasing and Decreasing Functions and the First Derivative Test
sectionTitles.3.4: Concavity and the Second Derivative Test

title: Integration
intro: Build integration from finite sums and connect accumulation to antiderivatives through the fundamental theorem.
prerequisites: Units 1–3: limits, derivatives and function behavior.

title: Logarithmic, Exponential, and Other Transcendental Functions
intro: Extend calculus to logarithms, exponentials, inverses and hyperbolic functions, and evaluate eligible indeterminate limits.
prerequisites: Units 2 and 4: chain rule, integration and substitution.

sectionTitles.5.5: Bases Other than e and Applications

title: Differential Equations
intro: Model change with differential equations and solve selected first-order equations analytically or numerically.

sectionTitles.6.3: Separation of Variables and the Logistic Equation

title: Applications of Integration
intro: Turn geometry and physical accumulation into integrals for area, volume, length, work, mass and fluid force.
prerequisites: Unit 4: definite integrals and substitution; Unit 5 for some applications.

sectionTitles.7.1: Area of a Region Between Two Curves
sectionTitles.7.4: Arc Length and Surfaces of Revolution
sectionTitles.7.6: Moments, Centers of Mass, and Centroids

title: Integration Techniques and Improper Integrals
intro: Choose integration methods and handle approximation, infinite intervals and singularities carefully.
prerequisites: Units 4–5: basic antiderivatives and transcendental functions.

sectionTitles.8.7: Integration by Tables and Other Integration Techniques

title: Infinite Series
intro: Study convergence, error control, power series and representation by Taylor and Maclaurin series.
prerequisites: Units 1–5 and 8: limits, derivatives, integrals and improper integrals.

sectionTitles.9.9: Representation of Functions by Power Series

title: Conics, Parametric Equations, and Polar Coordinates
intro: Use conics and new curve coordinates to calculate slopes, area, length and orbital geometry.
prerequisites: Units 2, 4–5 and 7–8: differentiation, integration and trigonometry.

sectionTitles.10.5: Area and Arc Length in Polar Coordinates
sectionTitles.10.6: Polar Equations of Conics and Kepler’s Laws

title: Vectors and the Geometry of Space
intro: Develop vector geometry, equations of lines and planes, quadric surfaces and spatial coordinate systems.
prerequisites: Preparation unit and Unit 10: algebra, trigonometry and coordinate geometry.

sectionTitles.11.2: Space Coordinates and Vectors in Space
sectionTitles.11.3: The Dot Product of Two Vectors
sectionTitles.11.4: The Cross Product of Two Vectors in Space

title: Vector-Valued Functions
intro: Differentiate and integrate vector-valued motion, then study tangent directions, speed and curvature.
prerequisites: Units 2, 4 and 11: calculus rules and vector operations.

sectionTitles.12.2: Differentiation and Integration of Vector-Valued Functions

title: Functions of Several Variables
intro: Extend limits and derivatives to several variables, and use gradients to linearize and optimize.
prerequisites: Units 1–3 and 11–12: limits, differentiation and spatial vectors.

sectionTitles.13.1: Introduction to Functions of Several Variables
sectionTitles.13.5: Chain Rules for Functions of Several Variables
sectionTitles.13.8: Extrema of Functions of Two Variables

title: Multiple Integration
intro: Integrate over regions and solids, choosing bounds and coordinate changes that match the geometry.
prerequisites: Units 4, 8, 11 and 13: integration, coordinates and partial derivatives.

sectionTitles.14.1: Iterated Integrals and Area in the Plane
sectionTitles.14.4: Center of Mass and Moments of Inertia

title: Vector Analysis
intro: Integrate fields along curves and over surfaces, connecting circulation, flux, curl and divergence.
prerequisites: Units 11–14: vector algebra, partial derivatives and multiple integration.

sectionTitles.15.3: Conservative Vector Fields and Independence of Path

title: Additional Topics in Differential Equations
intro: Extend differential equations to exact forms, second-order equations and power-series solutions. The PDF lists these online topics but does not include the chapter body.
prerequisites: Units 5–6 and 9: exponential functions, first-order equations and power series.
